tier_reason: The only external-baseline numbers are the author's own June 2016 blog post ('A clean C++11 deep learning API'), seen through WebSearch snippets only (blog.dlib.net fails DNS here); it gives ratios against Caffe with no network, batch size, GPU, Caffe version or flags tied to the comparison, and the dlib repo carries no Caffe benchmark code. First-party numbers without methodology are C.

corrections.workload: Deep neural network speed and GPU memory against Caffe on a GPU with dlib built on cuDNN v5 (author's June 2016 blog post 'A clean C++11 deep learning API', snippet only); the snippets give no network, batch size, GPU model for the comparison, or whether training or inference was timed.
corrections.caveats: Snippet only: blog.dlib.net could not be fetched (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so the numbers (fast mode about 1.6x Caffe's speed at about 1.5x the VRAM; low-VRAM mode about 0.85x Caffe's speed at about half the VRAM) come from WebSearch result text for the post https://blog.dlib.net/2016/06/a-clean-c11-deep-learning-api.html; the network, GPU, Caffe version, batch size and flags are unverified. A snippet mentions a ResNet34 model trained in about two weeks on a single Titan X GPU, but it is not clear that this GPU was the one used for the Caffe comparison. First-party author claim from 2016 against 2016-era Caffe and cuDNN v5; both have changed greatly since, and Caffe is no longer a current incumbent. The repo has no benchmark against Caffe or any other framework (README.md, docs/docs/ml.xml and docs/docs/release_notes.xml were checked); the release notes contain only dlib-versus-dlib speedups (CNN+MMOD detectors 2.5x faster) and a tools/convert_dlib_nets_to_caffe converter, so the comparison could be reproduced but is not checked in. Third-party reports in dlib GitHub discussions (video reading against OpenCV cv::VideoCapture) are mixed and trace mostly to thread-count defaults, so they do not support a speed win. The awesome-cpp baselines guess (system I/O or threading) was wrong for this project.

notes: Numbers match the WebSearch snippets of the specific post (benchmark_url corrected from the month archive to the post); tier C as a snippet-only, first-party, 2016 claim with no methodology. BSL-1.0, 14.5k stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-10-04 ('fix bug in unit test'), active. Category is a wave 8 category (autodiff-and-ml-kernels, domain numerics-and-science) although this record came from a wave 11 seed lead filed under filesystems-and-io; the orchestrator should keep the ML category or record a category override, since dlib has nothing in runtime-and-systems and is not already listed in wave 8.
